fix(pipeline): mark the step of an audience that did not render as failed, and say what became of the release notes
fix(cli): refuse a slip in --audience, refuse every argument alike, and close four small gaps in what a run says
fix(faithfulness): read a number with thousands separators as one number in the rule-based check
fix(cli): fit the line of a running step to the terminal's width, and keep the indent of doctor's details

renderings.technical:
### Added

- Render summaries in live terminals as formatted text, with bold headings and labels, colored code, and links displayed as their text. Preserve Markdown output for redirected, CI, and `--plain` output. ([#360](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/360))
- Place the spinner immediately before its step label, keep the status columns fixed when a step finishes, and align header values and their continuation lines at column nine. ([#352](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/352))

### Fixed

- Mark a step as failed when its audience does not render, then continue with the next audience. List release notes under `Skipped` when technical rendering fails or the technical audience is omitted. ([#359](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/359))
- Reject malformed audience lists and numeric audience values, validate `--repo` before displaying the run header, and give refused arguments consistent help guidance. Clarify the version command, output spacing, `--plain` help, and GitHub rate-limit message. ([#358](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/358))
- Compare numbers with thousands separators as a single number in the rule-based faithfulness check, removing commas for comparison while preserving text-based matching. ([#357](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/357))
- Fit running-step lines to the terminal width and preserve the indent when wrapping `doctor` details on a terminal. ([#356](https://github.com/goldbarth/chartula/pull/356))
renderings.customer:
### What's New

- **Terminal summaries:** On a live terminal, release summaries show headings, labels, code and links in a readable layout instead of Markdown source. This applies only to live terminal output, so redirected output, CI and `--plain` keep their existing Markdown form; the link text identifies the pull request, and its URL remains in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- **Progress display:** While a step runs, its spinner appears immediately before its label, and header values line up in a column. This applies to the terminal progress display; the finished status, label, count and time keep their positions, so you can follow each step without the spinner sitting apart from its label.

### Bug Fixes

- **Failed audience reporting:** When an audience fails to render, its step is marked as failed, and a publishing run lists the release notes under `Skipped` with the reason. This applies when an audience fails or is omitted, so the progress display and summary agree about what rendered and what happened to the notes.
- **Command-line errors:** Refused command-line arguments now show an error followed by a pointer to `chartula --help`, and an invalid `--repo` value is rejected before the run header appears. You can rely on the header appearing only for a run that started; use `chartula --version` to see the installed version.
- **Number checks:** The rule-based check now reads numbers such as `8,000` as a single number when comparing facts with a rendering. You can rely on thousands-separated numbers being compared without their commas, while versions such as `10.0.1` keep their existing comparison.
- **Terminal line wrapping:** Running-step lines now fit within the terminal width, and `doctor` details wrap between words while keeping their indent. On terminals narrower than ten columns, no running-step frame is drawn; when the terminal width cannot be read, the running-step line keeps its previous form, and plain `doctor` output remains unwrapped.
